10. Again referring the same case of Dr Nuul Islam vs Bangladesh, 33 DLR (AD) 201, he submits that the respondents neither took any steps under the impugned Rule 11(3) nor had they preferred any appeal against the judgment and order dated 11-9-2002 of the Administrative Tribunal within the statutory period of limitation, but long after about 4 (four) years they resorted to the impugned Rule 11 (3) in o mala fide intention to harass and humiliate the petitioner and, as such, impugned Memo Nos. Sal-AT-Opinion-31 / 2006/579 dated 23-7-2006 and DC: Bari/Uma-115/93/Nezarat-541 dated 28-8-2006 (Annexure-B) are liable to be declared to have been issued out of malice both in law and fact, without lawful authority and are of no legal effect. 

 12. In reply, the learned Advocate submits that the writ petition has been filed challenging the constitutionality of the impugned Rule 11(3) and the writ petition involves interpretation of Rule 11(3) as to whether it confers any unfettered and absolute discretion to the concerned authority to conduct any further or re-inquiry against any Government servant on the same allegation at anytime, whenever they wish or even after expiry of the statutory period of limitation for preferring any appeal before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal or any Appellate Court of law against the judgment and order of Administrative Tribunal or of a Court of law setting aside the penalty of dismissal, removal or compulsory retirement from service on the allegation and, as such, the writ petition is quite maintainable. 

 16. It appears from impugned Memo No. Sal/AT/Opinion-31 /2006-579 dated 23-7-2006 quoted before that as there was procedural defect in the departmental proceedings and as the appeal being barred by limitation it might be rejected, it was decided not to prefer any appeal on the condition of holding 're-inquiry' under Rule 11 (3) of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985 in the departmental proceedings against the petitioner. 

 (3) Where a penalty of dismissal, removal or compulsory retirement from service imposed upon a Government servant is set aside or declared or rendered void in consequence of, or by a decision of, a Court of law or Administrative Tribunal and the authority, on consideration of the circumstances of the case, decides to hold a further inquiry against him on the allegation on which the penalty of dismissal, removal or compulsory retirement was originally imposed the Government servant shall be deemed to have been placed under suspension by the authority from the date of original order of dismissal, removal as compulsory retirement and shall continue to remain under suspension until further orders. In such an eventuality, the limitation imposed under Rule 7(9) shall count from the date of decision to proceed against the accused following the Court decision. 

 19. Therefore, by making amendment to Rule 11 vide SRO 304-Law/89/EM (Rules-5) ID/88 dated 13-9-1989 the limitation clause for taking decision to hold further inquiry against any Government servant was omitted. Now, the question arises whether upon such omission the concerned authority has been legally authorized to take decision to hold such further inquiry at any time, whether they wish or event after the expiry of the statutory period 01 limitations under sub-sections (2) and (2A) of section 6 of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980 for preferring any appeal to the Administrative Appellate Tribunal against any order of decision of any Administrative Tribunal.
